meta.title: Our Process
meta.description: How a Rivya Living Art commission comes together — from the first WhatsApp conversation to layered pours, hand-finishing and tracked delivery across India.

hero.headline: From idea to heirloom.
hero.lead: Ten unhurried steps between your first message and the piece in your hands. Here is exactly how a Rivya Living Art commission comes together — and how long it honestly takes.

timeline.heading: Ten steps, no shortcuts
timeline.step1Copy: It starts with a WhatsApp conversation. You share the idea, reference photos, the sizes you're imagining and the budget you're comfortable with — and we ask the questions that shape the design, sketching it out before anything is poured.
timeline.step2Copy: Art-grade epoxy resin, mineral pigments, preserved florals and seasoned wood are matched to the brief — and, for a structural base, a 3D-printed form. If the piece holds your own flowers or keepsakes, we prepare and preserve them at this stage.
timeline.step3Copy: Seasoned teak and river wood is planed, sanded and sealed before it ever meets resin, so the grain is ready to hold a pour without warping or bubbling at the join.
timeline.step4Copy: Pigment is mixed into the resin in small batches and tested against the light before a full pour — gold leaf and preserved botanicals are set in only once the colour is right.
timeline.step5Copy: The composed resin is poured into the mould layer by layer, each one levelled and worked with a precision heat gun to clear air before it begins to set.
timeline.step6Copy: Each poured layer cures for 24–72 hours before the next goes in, and the finished piece rests under controlled conditions until it is fully hardened — resin rewards patience, not speed.
timeline.step4Meta: Nothing is poured before you approve
timeline.step1Alt: The studio bench at the start of a commission
timeline.step2Alt: An FDM print head laying translucent blue filament onto the build plate
timeline.step3Alt: Gold leaf flakes suspended in settling blue resin
timeline.step4Alt: Deep sapphire resin mid-pour, spreading across a round mould
timeline.step5Alt: Gloved hands working blue resin with a precision heat gun
timeline.step6Alt: Petals laid out in rows on paper and sorted with tweezers
timeline.step7Copy: Once fully cured, the piece is sanded from 400 up to 3000 grit, then polished until the surface reads like glass and the depth beneath it is fully clear.
timeline.step7Alt: A hand plane and curled shavings on a timber slab at the bench
timeline.step8Copy: Hardware, hooks or stands are fitted and checked by hand, and every edge is gone over once more before a piece is called finished.
timeline.step8Alt: Blue pigment swirling into clear resin in a beaker on a scale
timeline.step9Copy: The finished piece is checked edge to edge against the brief, and you receive photographs of it for your own approval before anything ships.
timeline.step9Alt: A sanding block resting on a wet-sanded resin surface
timeline.step10Copy: Once approved, the piece is packed fragile-proof and sent with tracked shipping, anywhere in India. The studio does not offer installation — delivery is where the commission ends.
timeline.step10Alt: A polishing pad buffing a cured resin surface to a gloss

meta.title: About
meta.description: The story of Rivya Living Art — a made-to-order resin art studio crafting ocean-blue, heirloom-grade pieces in India, one commission at a time.

hero.headline: Where resin meets reverence.
hero.lead: Rivya Living Art is a made-to-order resin art studio in Surat, India — a small practice devoted to holding what matters most in glass-clear depth: your wedding varmala, your photographs, your milestones.

story.heading: Our story
story.imageAlt: A preserved-flower resin frame handcrafted in the Rivya Living Art studio
story.p1: Rivya Living Art began as a one-artist studio — a single workbench and a quiet fascination with what happens when light passes through poured resin. It has grown commission by commission, yet it still works the way it started: one piece at a time, every stage passing through the same careful hands.
story.p2: The palette came from the sea. Sapphire, azure and deep-ocean blues run through nearly everything we make — colours with real depth, layered the way water layers light. Gold appears only as a garnish: a glint along an edge, a fine vein through the blue.
story.p3: We don't mass-produce, and we keep no inventory. Each commission begins as a conversation on WhatsApp — your idea, your references, your budget. A varmala to preserve after the wedding, a piece for the pooja room, a frame around one photograph — and it ends as a single object that exists nowhere else in the world.

values.heading: What we hold to
values.v1Copy: Resin cannot be rushed. Every layer cures on its own schedule, and we let it — clarity is the reward for waiting.
values.v2Copy: Your flowers, your photographs, your story. The materials that matter most arrive from your life, not a catalogue.
values.v3Copy: 3D printing meets hand-finishing — digital accuracy in the form, a human eye and hand on every surface.
values.v4Copy: Heirloom-grade materials and finishes, chosen so each piece can be kept, gifted and passed down.

craft.heading: Slow made, made once
craft.panel1Copy: Each layer settles for 24–72 hours before the next — resin rewards patience and punishes haste.
craft.panel2Copy: Slow cures keep the glass-clear depth free of bubbles and stress lines. We never rush a piece out of its mould.
craft.panel3Copy: From 400 to 3000 grit, then polish — until the surface disappears and only the ocean inside remains.

chapters.embedCopy: Flowers, gold leaf and keepsakes are placed by hand between layers — each element sealed exactly where it should rest, so the piece holds a moment and not just a material.
chapters.alt1: Deep sapphire resin pouring in one unbroken ribbon into a shallow round mould
chapters.alt2: Gold leaf flakes drifting inside settling translucent blue resin
chapters.alt3: Racks of filled moulds curing on steel shelves in the dark cure room
chapters.alt4: Water beading on a mirror-polished resin surface, gold flakes below

sustain.heading: Materials, chosen to endure
sustain.body: Museum-grade, UV-stable resin. Pigments and metals selected for how they age, not just how they photograph. And because every piece is made to order, nothing is overproduced — no inventory, no waste, just the pieces people asked us to make.

maker.heading: Rivya Living Art is led by Bhavya Gondaliya
maker.body: Every enquiry, sketch and pour passes through the maker's hands. When you message the studio, you are speaking with the person who will actually build your piece — no middle layer, no production line, just a conversation between you and your artist.
maker.name: Bhavya Gondaliya

intro.heading: An afternoon of colour, resin and quiet focus
intro.point1Copy: Sessions are kept intentionally small, so there's real one-on-one guidance at every table — never a crowd craning at a demo.
intro.point2Copy: Resin, pigments, moulds, tools, gloves and aprons are all laid out and waiting. Just bring yourself — and maybe a playlist request.
intro.point3Copy: No experience needed. First-timers are our favourite students, and private sessions can be arranged for any pace or occasion.

meta.title: Large-format resin art
meta.description: Commission large-format resin work in India — tables, surfaces, wall panels and sculptural pieces, designed around your room and poured to order.

hero.headline: Large resin art, made to your room.
hero.lead: A large piece is planned around a room before it is designed: where it sits, how it is used, how it gets through the door. That is why work at this scale begins as a conversation rather than an order.

scope.heading: Four kinds of large work
scope.intro: Scale changes the making, not the method. These are the shapes a large brief usually takes — yours does not have to be one of them.
scope.k1Copy: Dining and centre tables, counters, shelves and console tops — resin poured against seasoned wood, then levelled and polished by hand.
scope.k1Alt: A round coffee-table top mid-pour, clamped in a circular form as blue resin settles against the timber
scope.k2Copy: A single panel or a set that hangs together, poured to the proportions of the wall it is made for rather than to a standard frame size.
scope.k2Alt: A large resin wall panel leaning against a studio wall, a pale vein running through deep blue
scope.k3Copy: Free-standing forms, plinth pieces and light-catching blocks, built up in layers so the depth still reads from across a room.
scope.k3Alt: Poured resin moulds curing under a single warm work lamp in a dark studio
scope.k4Copy: Flowers, fabric and keepsakes set into a piece large enough to live with — prepared and stabilised first, then poured around.
scope.k4Alt: A stack of dated flower presses on the bench, pressed petals visible between the boards
scope.materials: Art-grade epoxy resin, mineral pigments, seasoned wood and preserved botanicals — the same materials as the small work, in more of it.

how.heading: Planned first, poured second
how.intro: The order of the work is what keeps a large piece from becoming a large mistake.
how.s1Copy: You send the space, the use and whatever measurements you already have. We ask about the way in, what it will stand on, and who else has to agree.
how.s2Copy: Sketches, and a digital preview where one helps. Nothing is poured until the design, the finish and the size are agreed between us.
how.s3Copy: Resin goes in layer by layer, each one left to cure before the next. Large work has more layers, and that is the part of the calendar nobody can compress.
how.s4Copy: Sanded, polished and fitted with the hardware it needs to stand or hang. You see photographs of the finished piece, and how it travels is agreed before it leaves the studio.

brief.heading: What makes a quote quick
brief.intro: None of this has to be exact. Rough numbers and a phone photograph are enough to start.
brief.b1Copy: A photograph of the wall, corner or floor the piece is for, taken from where you usually stand.
brief.b2Copy: Length, width and height if you know them — and the narrowest doorway, stair or lift between the street and the room.
brief.b3Copy: Daily dining, a display piece, an office reception — use decides thickness, finish and edge more than taste does.
brief.b4Copy: Colours, grain, photographs of work you like, or the piece you keep imagining and cannot find anywhere.
brief.disclaimer: No payment is taken here. Materials, price and dates are confirmed with you on WhatsApp before anything begins.

gallery.heading: Pieces at this scale
gallery.intro: Work the studio has grouped as large-format. Where a size or a material is recorded for a piece, it is printed with it.
gallery.emptyHeading: Documented as they leave the studio
gallery.emptyBody: There is nothing to browse at this scale yet. The conversation does not wait for the gallery — describe the piece you want and we will design it from the room outwards.

cta.heading: Tell us about the room
cta.body: Send the space, the use and the date that matters. Design, materials and price are settled with you on WhatsApp before a single layer is poured.

philosophy.heading: Planned before it is priced
philosophy.p1: A large piece lives with a room for years, so it is designed for that room specifically — never sized to a standard sheet and shipped out.
philosophy.p2: The studio takes on a small number of large commissions at a time, for the same reason each one takes weeks rather than days: layered resin work at this scale cannot be rushed without it showing later.
philosophy.p3: Nothing is poured until the design, the finish and the size are agreed in writing — the room gets one chance to be measured correctly, and the studio does not guess.
